name: Mizuna edible-leaf microbial load (VEG-04A/B)
task: Culturable aerobic microbial load regression on edible leaf tissue
sourceType: NASA OSDR ALSDA plate-count measurement tables (LSDS-128)
method: NASA-data-trained exploratory regression (ridge / random forest comparison)
target: log10(1 + CFU per gram fresh leaf weight)

evidenceBasis.rule: validated-exploratory requires beating the baseline, positive R2 on every leave-one-experiment-out holdout, and conformal empirical coverage within 5 points of nominal. Otherwise the model is reported as experimental.

recommendedUse: Descriptive in-campaign microbial-load stratification only. Do NOT use to predict a new mission, a different cultivar or a different hardware configuration: leave-one-experiment-out R2 is negative for both campaigns.
validation: 4-fold GroupKFold grouped by pillow (biological replicate), with a nested 3-fold grouped alpha search. Gene-to-fold leakage is impossible because all samples from one pillow stay in one fold. A separate leave-one-experiment-out diagnostic holds out an entire VEG-04A or VEG-04B campaign.

interval.kind: UNCALIBRATED descriptive residual range, log10 CFU/g (empirical coverage below nominal; not a confidence interval)

limitations: Plate counts capture only culturable aerobic organisms; total microbial load is higher and unmeasured.
The target is microbial load on leaf tissue. It is NOT biomass, yield, growth rate or shelf life.
freshWeightG is the mass of the tissue subsample taken for the assay, not harvest biomass.
VEG-04A and VEG-04B differ in design; the leave-one-experiment-out errors show how poorly the effect transfers and must be read before use.
Two experimental campaigns only, both VEG-04 mizuna on ISS. No lettuce, tomato or radish transfer.
Flight/ground differences may reflect cabin environment, payload handling or sampling protocol, not gravity per se. Causality is not established.
Not a food-safety clearance tool. Do not use for consumption decisions.
